sections.html:
Mississippi's capital and most populous city, Jackson, lies on the Pearl River in the center of the state. Most of it lies in northeastern Hinds County, where it shares the county seat role with Raymond. Slivers extend into Rankin County, home to the airport, and Madison County, home to Tougaloo College.

At about 113 square miles, Jackson is big and uneven. Ridgeland is north, Flowood and Richland are east, Byram is south and Clinton is west. Interstates 55 and 20 meet near downtown, with Interstate 220 and U.S. 49, 51 and 80 filling out the grid. Downtown's Union Station serves Amtrak's City of New Orleans along with Greyhound and the city's buses.

Public schools are mostly run by Jackson Public Schools, but some Hinds County addresses fall into other districts. If a buyer asks which district serves your address, check rather than guess.

The 2020 census recorded 153,701 residents, down 11.42 percent from 173,514 in 2010. In a city that has shrunk, the street you live on counts for a lot, and two houses a mile apart can sell on very different terms.

sections.h2: Jackson's water system and your sale
sections.html:
A federal court supervises the city's water system. More than 71,000 connections depend on it, and repairs are still under way at both treatment plants and across the distribution network. When the system failed in 2022, tens of thousands of people went without running water for weeks.

On November 29, 2022 the court entered an Interim Stipulated Order agreed to by the EPA, the Department of Justice, the Mississippi State Department of Health and the City. It put an Interim Third-Party Manager in charge of operations, working through JXN Water, with a list of priority projects. Fixes to distribution leaks have cut average daily demand by 25 percent, and corrosion control treatment is finished at the J.H. Fewell plant.

Expect buyers to ask about pressure, boil water notices and plumbing. Hold on to recent water bills, jot down any past notices you remember, and answer plainly. JXN Water posts billing, customer service and boil water information, and the Health Department posts compliance reports. A cash buyer who takes the house as is does not need your plumbing to satisfy a lender.

Storms, rain and soil are what buyers' inspectors tend to chase in Jackson. Much of the city sits on acidic silt loam, and the Pearl River runs along the east side with the Ross Barnett Reservoir to the northeast.

  • A roof's hail and wind claim history is part of the house's record, so keep the claim paperwork.
  • Foundation movement and poor drainage are frequent reasons buyers ask for credits in silty soil.
  • Look up the flood designation before you guess at insurance costs, especially near the river or a creek.

The Office of Code Services applies the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code with local changes. Its Community Improvement division aims for voluntary compliance, goes to court as a last resort, and spends federal, state and local money to repair violations on properties held by absentee owners. Eight enforcement beats cover the city, each with its own officer.

The city council passes resolutions declaring particular parcels a menace to public health, safety and welfare under Section 21-19-11 of the Mississippi Code, then authorizes cleanup or demolition. Call the code office and ask whether costs for either have been assessed against your parcel.

Landlords have another duty. Jackson relaunched rental registration, which calls for a local agent who can act for the owner and produces a Rental Certificate. Rentals now outnumber owner-occupied homes in the city. Make sure a rental house is registered before you sell, and tell any buyer if it is not.

sections.h2: Hinds County tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
The county mails statements during the first week of December. Full payment is due on or before February 1, and each month after that adds a half percent penalty, even on installments. The postmark decides whether you were late. If no bill arrives, call the county tax collector at (601) 968-6591.

The statement carries the name of whoever owned the property on January 1, which is why a buyer may see a previous owner's name on a receipt. Title companies normally divide the year's tax between buyer and seller at closing.

Tax ruleHinds County detail
Statements mailedFirst week of December
Payment dueOn or before February 1
Late penalty0.5 percent per month, including installments
Name on statementOwner as of January 1
Owner-occupied single-family assessment10 percent of true value
Other real property assessment15 percent of true value
State tax sale datesFirst Monday in April and last Monday in August

Delinquent parcels can be sold at the tax sale, and Hinds County publishes both a delinquent list and a tax sale list. State law permits sales on the first Monday in April and the last Monday in August. Call the tax collector for the current schedule, and ask for a payoff figure early so the balance can come out of your sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Jackson house quickly
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell it yourself or take a cash offer. Which one works often depends on the property's condition and paperwork. Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code call for a covered seller to hand over a written property condition disclosure statement before title passes. Be accurate, because buyers may ask about water service and storm history.

Cash sales are common for inherited houses, vacant houses, houses with open code cases and rentals with registration problems. A cash buyer can take the house as is and deal with city notices afterward, but you still pay liens from the proceeds and tell the buyer about violations you know of.

If the house has a water or plumbing history, tell the buyer up front. A repair the buyer learns about from you is a negotiating point. A repair the buyer finds on a closing-week inspection can stall the deal or end it.

Compare offers by what you keep, not by the number on the front page. Get terms in writing, ask who covers closing costs, and take your time. We make no price promises, and you can turn any offer down.

sections.h2: What to have ready for a closing
sections.html: A Jackson sale usually runs in four steps: contract, title search, payoff, signing. Nothing about that order changes with a cash buyer, though the lender's appraisal and approval stage drops out. The title search lists liens, unpaid taxes and any city assessments, so you learn early what has to be paid from the proceeds. Bring identification, your mortgage payoff details if you have a loan, recent water bills, and records of past repairs or insurance claims. If a rental is involved, bring proof of registration and the Rental Certificate.

faqs.a: Most of Jackson is in Hinds County, where it shares the county seat with Raymond. Small portions reach into Rankin County and Madison County.

faqs.q: When are Hinds County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due on or before February 1. After that date a half percent penalty applies each month, and a postmark after February 1 counts as late.

faqs.q: Does the water situation affect selling a Jackson house?
faqs.a: Buyers may ask about it. A court-ordered manager runs the system, repairs continue, and JXN Water posts boil water notices. Keep your bills and answer questions honestly.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Jackson before selling it?
faqs.a: The city requires rental registration and issues a Rental Certificate. Check your status with the Office of Code Services and tell a buyer about any problem.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jackson house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Open violations and any city cleanup liens are usually settled from the proceeds at closing, so ask the code office what is outstanding. An as-is cash sale is a common way to handle it.
